newsitem.title: CONGO: Archbishop Monsengwo in Congo on way back to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Archbishop Monsengwo in Congo on way back to Zaire.

text.p: Archbishop Laurent Monsengwo, tipped by some as a key player in any peaceful settlement to Zaire's civil war, arrived in Congo on Monday on his way back to his troubled country.
Monsengwo, elected to his old job of speaker of Zaire's transitional parliament by supporters of embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko, declined comment on whether he would take the job.
"I'm not making any statements here. I will give a press conference in Kinshasa," he told journalists in Congo's capital Brazzaville.
Zaire's rebels, who control three quarters of the huge nation, have told Monsengwo not to take the job and have threatened to attack the capital Kinshasa if he does.

Zaire's radical opposition, the other major political force in parliament, walked out during Saturday's vote and rejected the nomination of Monsengwo as speaker -- the constitutional successor to Mobutu in the event of death or incapacity.

Monsengwo, archbishop of Zaire's rebel-held third city of Kisangani, is still popular in a country with a Roman Catholic majority. He held the job of speaker at the height of Zaire's promised transition to democracy.

Some diplomats and politicians say Monsengwo could step in and provide Mobutu with a dignified exit. Others say Monsengwo could act as a national mediator -- a role he played as speaker until ousted in July 1995.

"I will only accept if I have national and international guarantees," Monsengwo told a news conference in Belgium during a stopover on his way back to Kinshasa from the Vatican where he attended a conference. He did not elaborate.

The Vatican has yet to give its blessing to the move but Monsengwo promised initiatives to find a peaceful settlement. He gave no details but said these aimed "at a transition which has consensus support and is quick".

Mobutu supporters, fearing Monsengwo's popularity in the event of elections, joined forces with Tshisekedi supporters in 1995 to oust him. Tshisekedi supporters dismiss Monsengwo, archbishop of rebel-held Kisangani, as "Mobutist".
Monsengwo arrived in Congo by plane from Brussels and went for a meeting with members of the Congolese church.
Family members in Kinshasa said he would return to Zaire on Monday or Tuesday.
